title: Counting Bits
statement:
For every number from 0 to `n`, count how many bits are set to 1 when it is written in binary. For example, 5 is `101` in binary, so it has two 1 bits.

The input is one integer `n`, where `0 <= n <= 10^5`. Print `n + 1` counts on one line, separated by spaces: the count for 0, then for 1, and so on up to `n`. Try to work out each count in one step from a count you already have, instead of looking at every bit of every number.

Input:

```text
5
```

Expected output:

```text
0 1 1 2 1 2
```
hints: Fill a list of counts in increasing order, starting with 0 for the number 0.
`i >> 1` is `i` with its lowest bit dropped. It is smaller than `i`, so you already have its count, and it has the same 1 bits as `i` apart from that lowest one.
`i & 1` is 1 when the lowest bit of `i` is set, so add it back to the count for `i >> 1`.

python.solution:
def count_bits(n: int) -> list[int]:
    bits = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1)
    return bits


n = int(input())
print(" ".join(str(x) for x in count_bits(n)))
